title: Sinus CT scan
also: CT scan of the nose and sinuses
what: Cross-section images of your nose and sinuses. They show swelling, fluid, polyps, and the structure of the nose.
why: For frequent or long-lasting sinusitis, before nose surgery, or when an X-ray gave no clear answer.
duration: usually 5 to 10 minutes in the room; the scan itself takes a few seconds; the report the same day or in 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: If you are or might be pregnant
If you had a sinus X-ray or CT before. Bring the images

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: Usually none. Contrast dye is rarely used for the sinuses. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Take off earrings, hair clips, glasses, removable dentures, and hearing aids.

steps: You lie on the table, and the technician helps you get comfortable
The table moves into the wide ring of the scanner
Your head rests in a holder, sometimes while you lie on your stomach
Do not move or swallow for a few seconds
feel: It does not hurt. The scanner hums quietly
The ring is wide, so it does not feel cramped
after: You can go about your day right away
Take the report and images to your ENT doctor

faq.q: Why is a sinus CT better than an X-ray?
faq.a: CT shows all the sinuses and their passages in detail. This matters before surgery and in complex cases.

faq.q: Can I have a sinus CT with a runny nose?
faq.a: Yes. But if the CT is planned, your doctor may ask you to have it after a cold has cleared.

reminders.text: Sinus CT soon. Take off earrings and hair clips, and bring past images.
